successCriteria.description: `PgLeaveRequestRepository.findByQuery` honors `params.employeeIds`: when present and non-empty it adds an `employee_id = ANY($n)` condition with the array passed as a single bound parameter, and when absent/empty it applies no employee filter (ADMIN sees all).

`ILeaveService` exposes `list(actor, params)` and `getById(actor, requestId)` and `LeaveService` implements both; `list` scopes `employeeIds` by role (EMPLOYEE → `[actor.id]`; MANAGER → `[actor.id, ...directReportIds]` via `employeeService.getEmployeesByManagerId`, one level only; ADMIN → no filter) and delegates the actual query to the repository (no SQL in the service).

`getById` loads via `repository.findById` and applies the SAME role-scoped visibility rule as `list`; a request the caller may not see throws `NotFoundError('Leave request not found')` — byte-for-byte identical to a nonexistent id, so the endpoint cannot probe ids.
Reads are status-unrestricted: a MANAGER sees direct reports' requests in EVERY status (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED), and neither `list` nor `getById` filters or rejects on `status`.

The read routes parse wire query params: `status`/`leaveTypeCode` validated against their enums (invalid → ValidationError), `startDateFrom`/`startDateTo`/`endDateFrom`/`endDateTo` converted from strings to `Date` (invalid → ValidationError, mirroring `parseCreateBody`), and `limit`/`offset` as integers; the handler resolves the actor via the existing `resolveActor` and returns the service result.
Neither `list` nor `getById` opens a transaction or forwards a client; both are read-only and perform no writes, no audit records, and no notifications.

constraints: No SQL in the service layer — the `employeeIds` filter is expressed only inside `PgLeaveRequestRepository.findByQuery`; `LeaveService.list` builds the `employeeIds` array and passes it through `LeaveRequestQueryParams`.
Read endpoints must not open a transaction (no `uow.withTransaction`, no client forwarding) — this phase is read-only.
No new exports from `src/modules/leave/index.ts` — `ILeaveService` is already exported and the new methods ride on it.
No controller file is introduced — routes call the service directly, matching the existing `leave.routes.ts` shape.
No shared-type change is permitted this phase — `LeaveRequestQueryParams.employeeIds` already exists (Phase 1) and must be reused as-is.
outOfScope: No writes, audit records, or notifications — this phase is strictly read-only; state-changing operations (create/submit/approve/reject/cancel) are untouched.
No smoke.js changes or end-to-end probes — those belong to Phase 7.
No refactor of `leave.service.ts`/`balance.service.ts` to import the shared date helpers — deferred to a later phase.
No promotion of `LeavePolicyStatus` into shared types and no controller-layer introduction — both are separate concerns outside this phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: Visibility is role-scoped and status-unrestricted: EMPLOYEE sees only their own requests; MANAGER sees their own plus direct reports (employee.managerId === actor.id), one level only, not transitive; ADMIN sees all. The same rule governs both list and single-read, and a request the caller may not see is indistinguishable from a nonexistent one (404).
Reads never mutate lifecycle state: `list`/`getById` return the persisted row unchanged and do not alter `status`, `approverId`, `decidedAt`, `cancelledBy`, `cancelledAt`, or any balance counters.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Actor must be authenticated (missing/invalid → UnauthorizedError/ForbiddenError via the existing assertAuthenticated); visibility is role-scoped (EMPLOYEE self, MANAGER self+direct reports, ADMIN all).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only; returns an array (possibly empty); no NotFoundError for an empty result set.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Actor must be authenticated; visibility is role-scoped with the same rule as list.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: NotFoundError('Leave request not found') for both a nonexistent id and an id the caller may not see (identical 404, no id probing).

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the existing `resolveActor` and `sendError` helper shape from `leave.routes.ts` for the new read routes so error mapping stays identical across modules.
Reuse the existing `parseCreateBody` date-conversion pattern (`new Date(value)` + `Number.isNaN(parsed.getTime())` → ValidationError) for the date query params.
Reuse `LeaveRequestQueryParams` (including its existing `employeeIds?: string[]`) and the `LeaveStatus`/`LeaveTypeCode` enums from shared types — do not re-declare or diverge.
Reuse `IEmployeeService.getEmployeesByManagerId(actor.id)` (returns `[]` for an unknown manager) to derive MANAGER direct reports — one level only, no transitive expansion.
Reuse the existing `NotFoundError` type and its `'Leave request not found'` message so the invisible-id and nonexistent-id cases are byte-identical.

integrationPoints.why: MANAGER role scoping derives the direct-report id list (one level only) for the `employeeIds` filter.
The service delegates all data access to the repository; `findByQuery` applies the `employeeIds` ANY($n) filter and `findById` supplies the row for `getById` visibility checks.
The wire query params map onto this existing DTO (status, leaveTypeCode, date ranges, employeeIds, limit, offset) — the contract between routes and service.
